The manual choice replaced the shared URL state.

A direct preview navigation to /#/law/BWBR0001854?revision=abc&section=1&place=place:amsterdam&scope=place kept that hash, showed place:amsterdam with origin shared URL, data-state screen-reader-scope-change, and main text Law BWBR0001854. Requesting /law/BWBR0001854?revision=abc&section=1 returned the sealed 404.html, and its current-route script replaced the location with /#/law/BWBR0001854?revision=abc&section=1, which rendered the same record id. /index.html#/law/BWBR0001854 kept hash #/law/BWBR0001854 and rendered BWBR0001854. Nine redirect cases were checked while sealing 404.html, including /search?q=parking and an existing hash law link. On the public host, Chrome showed the statute JSON at its direct Pages path and the GitHub 404 at https://worldwidelaws.github.io/#/search.

The preview document for /#/search and the dated law route /#/law/BWBR0001854?place=place:amsterdam&date=2026-10-26&scope=place both mounted the worldwide shell. Response headers had no Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and no Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy. In Chrome, crossOriginIsolated was false and SharedArrayBuffer was absent. Recorded hosts were 127.0.0.1:4179 and plausible.io. The plausible script is the analytics tag copied into index.html. No request went to Convex, OpenRouter, or country.is. https://worldwidelaws.github.io/ returned GitHub's static 404 page and did not start an application server. The shell remained usable with searched count 0.

The sealed preview route /#/coverage rendered heading Coverage, data-coverage unknown, text Coverage: Coverage unknown, and zero result rows. It did not claim that every law was collected.
